title.narrative: Child labour risk factors profiling and mitigation plans in coffee supply chains in Huehuetenango, Guatemala

description.narrative: Child labour is widely recognized as endemic to the agriculture sector in Guatemala. Although national laws have been put in place to deter these practices, compliance with the laws is insufficient. Thus, each year, children are exposed to physically and emotionally harmful work on coffee farms. Child labour is a complex issue caused by multiple factors and exacerbated by the social, economic, and political realities of the country. Project A involves collecting this information through surveys with key informers, government, non-governmental organisations (NGOs), private partners at national, regional, local level, combined with an appropriate sample of household surveys in target communities and interviews with children. Based on the findings from Project A, Project B will adopt a landscape approach to tackle root causes of child labour in Huehuetenango through a collaboration of Anacafe and Funcafe, local government, Mercon, Peet’s, Rainforest Alliance (RA), and Seeds for Progress, while in parallel also strengthening the due diligence systems of Mercon B.V. and Peet’s Coffee.

The Rainforest Alliance is committed to the eradication of child labour and promotes prevention, remediation and monitoring, tailored to local contexts and risks through its Sustainable Agriculture Standard and its landscapes & communities work. Mercon has a purpose of building a better coffee world and its future is tied to better opportunities for children in rural areas to prepare them to face the challenges ahead of us. Mercon has zero tolerance for child labour in their supply chains and they continuously work to detect and mitigate any occurrence. They have set an ambitious target of 100% sustainable sourcing by 2030. Peet’s wishes to address the risk of child labour because this is part of what it means to be a responsible corporate citizen and engaged community member; they want to do their part to ensure the next generation can realize its full potential. From a stakeholder perspective, Peet’s employees, customers, investors, and others expect them to do their part to address this risk and many other sustainability-focused topics.

comment.narrative: 250 farmers trained on Intercropping with Coffee 50 farmers diversifying livelihood to increase the incomes
This is the total target of the project

During the reporting period, 68 producers began training under the Sustainable Profitability curriculum, including modules related to improved agronomic practices and diversification. Additional trainings on intercropping and livelihood diversification are planned for 2026 to reach the full target.

title.narrative: Number of people (from the target group) enrolled in formal or non-formal education and training - Total

comment.narrative: This is the total target for the project

By December 2025, 10 Extra-Curricular Middle School (ECMS) centers were established and operational, enrolling 218 adolescents, including strong female participation. Enrollment exceeded the original target of 200 youth, reflecting high community demand for alternative education pathways in areas lacking secondary schools.

title.narrative: Number of children in formal or non-formal education and training, at any level, by sex and age - Total

comment.narrative: Children in coffeecamps and kindergartens during harvesting season aged 5 - 13
This is the total target for the project

During the reporting period, 6 Coffee Kindergarten/Camp programs were inaugurated and became operational in selected communities. A total of 136 children aged 5–13 were enrolled, exceeding the initial annual target. These safe learning spaces are designed to operate during peak harvest periods to reduce children’s exposure to hazardous work and will continue through the next harvest cycle.
